headline: Looped diffusion language models report lower training FLOPs and adaptive inference savings
summary: The preprint studies selective recurrence inside uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs), repeatedly applying a shared two-block slice of the denoiser without adding parameters. The authors report that looped models reach the non-looped model's validation negative log-likelihood with up to 2.8× fewer training FLOPs on OpenWebText and 3.3× fewer on FineWeb-Edu. At matched denoiser-evaluation budgets, they report up to 9.8% lower generation perplexity; an adaptive stopping rule matches fixed-depth multiple-choice accuracy while using 26.0%–34.8% fewer loop traversals. These results come from a 12-block, hidden-size-768 model on two corpora and remain unreplicated independently; larger-scale quality, wall-clock and dollar savings are unknown.
